public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is almost zero chance that AGI, meaning a system that can do almost any cognitive task a human can do, will arrive within the next two to three years.
public_payload.original_horizon_text: in the next two to three years

statement.excerpt: I think there is almost zero chance that artificial general intelligence (which his podcast guest reasonably defines as “a system capable of doing almost any cognitive task a human can do“) will arrive in the next two to three years, especially given how disappointing GPT 4.5 turned out to be.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

from_speaker: a system capable of doing almost any cognitive task a human can do
in the next two to three years
our_interpretation: The latest deadline is March 5, 2028, three years after publication.
Arrival means the existence of a working system meeting the stated breadth of cognitive capability. A company calling its system AGI is insufficient.
Human comparisons must cover varied cognitive activities, including unfamiliar tasks. Marcus supplies no numerical meaning for almost any.
This assessment concerns whether the forecast event occurs. One outcome cannot establish whether an almost-zero probability was well calibrated.
criteria.support_condition: After March 5, 2028, sufficiently comprehensive evidence establishes that no system meeting the stated definition arrived within the forecast interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A working system meeting the stated definition is demonstrated to have existed by March 5, 2028, with credible independent evaluation of its breadth.
